newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler says forex changes boosted 96 sales.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says forex changes boosted 96 sales.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG chief financial office Manfred Gentz said on Wednesday that foreign exchange rate changes added 1.4 billion marks to the group's revenue in 1996.
In the text of a speech, Gentz said the impact on operating profit from currency market swings, however, was only 400 million marks.

"We had to report significant shortfalls in revenues and earnings in 1995 as a result of the revaluation of the German mark as compared to other important currencies," Gentz said. "The situation changed for the better in 1996."
The CFO added that because of U.S. accounting standards under which Daimler figures its books, the climb of the mark had a negative impact on net income.
Hedging transactions, Gentz said, have to be evaluated on every balance sheet date, creating expenses or income for the financial results, in Daimler's case last year hurting net income.
